## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Ñāṇathavikattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 486) is a biographical verse text preserved in the Therāpadāna of the Pali Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. Secondary scholarship citing this text identifies it with the narrative of the ascetic Sumedha resolving to pursue buddhahood before the Buddha Dīpaṅkara rather than attaining immediate nirvāṇa [Karuna in indian buddhist lit]. In this connection, Maurice Winternitz notes that E. Müller compared the Dīpaṅkara account in this Apadāna with parallel versions, suggesting contact with Kumāralāta's *Kalpanāmaṇḍitikā*, though Winternitz concluded that the Apadāna preserves a simpler, unelaborated narrative that likely served as source material [Winternitz 1933].

SuttaCentral records five modern translations of the text in five languages [SuttaCentral]. Computational text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus shows extensive internal Pali reuse across 280 matches in 55 texts, most prominently with the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā* (matching segments §0.3–28.1 and §12.3–15.1) and the *Therīgāthā-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. The text also shares standard verse formulas with numerous other poems in the collection, such as the *Sabbadāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 401), the *Yāgudāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 420), the *Ajitattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 402), and the *Sāriputtattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 3) [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language matches, DharmaNexus automatically aligns segments of the text (such as §11.3) with Tibetan translations of the Mahāyāna *Suvarṇaprabhāsottamasūtra* [DharmaNexus].
